evals.prompt: /jira-cli show me my open high-priority bugs in a format I can parse in a script
assertions: Runs `jira version` (or states it was already confirmed this session) before running any issue query, to confirm the binary is ankitpokhrel/jira-cli

Constructs a `jira issue list` command with assignee/type/priority/status filters (e.g. `-a$(jira me) -tBug -yHigh -s~Done`) using `--plain` (and typically `--no-headers`) rather than the default interactive table
Executes the actual `jira` command rather than fabricating issue keys or summaries
Reports only issues that appear in the real command's output, with no invented ticket IDs

evals.prompt: /jira-cli move every one of my 'To Do' issues into 'In Progress'
assertions: First runs a read-only `jira issue list` (e.g. `-a$(jira me) -s"To Do" --plain --columns key --no-headers`) to enumerate the real issue keys before mutating anything
Loops the mutating `jira issue move <KEY> "In Progress"` command over the keys returned by that list rather than a hardcoded or guessed set of keys
Reports a count of issues moved that is derived from the actual list/loop output, not an invented number
States the plan (which keys, which transition) before or alongside running the bulk move rather than silently mutating every ticket with no visibility

evals.prompt: /jira-cli list my assigned issues (note: `jira version` in this shell prints output for an unrelated tool, not ankitpokhrel/jira-cli)
assertions: Runs `jira version` before attempting any issue/epic/sprint command
Detects that the version output does not match ankitpokhrel/jira-cli and stops instead of proceeding
Does not run any `jira issue`, `jira epic`, or `jira sprint` command after detecting the mismatch
Final message reports the binary mismatch and suggests checking `which jira`, without inventing any issue data
